chapters.title: External Data Sources
chapters.subtitle: Elasticsearch, Azure AI Search and PostgreSQL

steps.text: Not all knowledge lives in your site's content index. Some of it is in a search index that another system maintains, or in a database table. This video shows data sources that read Elasticsearch, Azure AI Search and PostgreSQL.

chapters.title: Why external sources
chapters.subtitle: Read the knowledge where it is

steps.text: A search index or a database that another team keeps up to date is knowledge already. Copying it into your site by hand would only go stale.
An external data source reads it where it is, splits it into passages, and keeps your knowledge base in step.
Elasticsearch, Azure AI Search and PostgreSQL each have their own source type. Everything after the connection is the same as for any data source.

chapters.title: What every source shares
chapters.subtitle: A connection, a destination, a mapping

steps.text: The connection settings tell the site where to read: the index and its address, or the database and its table. Your technical team provides them.
The destination is a knowledge base index of your site, the same one that every data source stores its passages in.
The field mapping names the fields that hold the content, the title and the key. Here you type the names, because the site cannot list the fields of a remote source.
Open Artificial Intelligence, Data Sources, click Add Data Source, and click Add on Elasticsearch.
Enter a Name, and the Index name, which is the name of the index on the other server.
Choose the Environment type. Self-managed asks for the Elasticsearch URL. Choose the Authentication type your technical team gives you: none, a user name and password, or an API key.
Choose the Destination index, the knowledge base index of your site. It cannot be changed after you save.
In Field Mapping, type the Content field, the Title field and the Key field, as they are named in the remote index.
Click Save. The data source reads the remote index, and fills its knowledge base in the background.

chapters.title: Ask a question
chapters.subtitle: An answer from the external index

steps.text: Choose the data source on a profile, on the Knowledge tab, exactly as for any data source.
Then ask a question that the remote notes answer: how do I reset the router?
The assistant answers from the remote index, and the numbered source shows the note it used.

chapters.title: An Azure AI Search data source
chapters.subtitle: Read an Azure AI Search index

steps.text: An Azure AI Search data source asks for a Name, the Index name, and the Endpoint of the search service.
Authentication offers an API key, which is stored securely and never shown again, or an identity, with the Client ID of a managed identity.
The Destination index and the Field Mapping work as before. Azure AI Search does not support the Filter of a profile.
A PostgreSQL data source asks for a Name, and the Connection string of the database. The connection string is stored securely, and never shown again.
The Table name is the table to read. In Field Mapping, the content, title and key fields are the names of columns of that table.
A search index that a product team already maintains, for support answers.
An Azure AI Search index of manuals, shared by several applications.
A database table of articles or notes, read without a copy.
Point a data source at the index or table where the knowledge already lives, map its fields, and choose it on a profile. Thanks for watching.
